verses.text: The two angels came to Sodom at evening. Lot sat in the gate of Sodom. Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them. He bowed himself with his face to the earth,

and he said, “See now, my lords, please turn aside into your servant’s house, stay all night, wash your feet, and you can rise up early, and go on your way.” They said, “No, but we will stay in the street all night.”
He urged them greatly, and they came in with him, and entered into his house. He made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, both young and old, all the people from every quarter.
They called to Lot, and said to him, “Where are the men who came in to you this night? Bring them out to us, that we may have sex with them.”
Lot went out to them to the door, and shut the door after him.
He said, “Please, my brothers, don’t act so wickedly.

See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them what seems good to you. Only don’t do anything to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.”

They said, “Stand back!” Then they said, “This one fellow came in to live as a foreigner, and he appoints himself a judge. Now will we deal worse with you, than with them!” They pressed hard on the man Lot, and came near to break the door.
But the men reached out their hand, and brought Lot into the house to them, and shut the door.
They struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.
The men said to Lot, “Do you have anybody else here? Sons-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and whoever you have in the city, bring them out of the place:
for we will destroy this place, because the outcry against them has grown so great before Yahweh that Yahweh has sent us to destroy it.”

Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters, and said, “Get up! Get out of this place, for Yahweh will destroy the city.” But he seemed to his sons-in-law to be joking.
When the morning came, then the angels hurried Lot, saying, “Get up! Take your wife, and your two daughters who are here, lest you be consumed in the iniquity of the city.”
But he lingered; and the men grabbed his hand, his wife’s hand, and his two daughters’ hands, Yahweh being merciful to him; and they took him out, and set him outside of the city.
It came to pass, when they had taken them out, that he said, “Escape for your life! Don’t look behind you, and don’t stay anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountains, lest you be consumed!”
Lot said to them, “Oh, not so, my lord.

See now, your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have magnified your loving kindness, which you have shown to me in saving my life. I can’t escape to the mountain, lest evil overtake me, and I die.
See now, this city is near to flee to, and it is a little one. Oh let me escape there (isn’t it a little one?), and my soul will live.”
He said to him, “Behold, I have granted your request concerning this thing also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
Hurry, escape there, for I can’t do anything until you get there.” Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.
The sun had risen on the earth when Lot came to Zoar.
Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.
He overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew on the ground.
But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham got up early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Yahweh.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and looked, and saw that the smoke of the land went up as the smoke of a furnace.
When God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the middle of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Lot lived.
Lot went up out of Zoar, and lived in the mountain, and his two daughters with him; for he was afraid to live in Zoar. He lived in a cave with his two daughters.
The firstborn said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in to us in the way of all the earth.
Come, let’s make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve our father’s family line .”
They made their father drink wine that night: and the firstborn went in, and lay with her father. He didn’t know when she lay down, nor when she arose.

It came to pass on the next day, that the firstborn said to the younger, “Behold, I lay last night with my father. Let us make him drink wine again, tonight. You go in, and lie with him, that we may preserve our father’s family line. ”
They made their father drink wine that night also. The younger went and lay with him. He didn’t know when she lay down, nor when she got up.
Thus both of Lot’s daughters were with child by their father.
The firstborn bore a son, and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger also bore a son, and called his name Ben Ammi. He is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.

footnotes.content: I see Lot sitting in the gate of Sodom, the place where men of influence would be found. Even so, when two angels appeared, he rose to meet them and bowed low. It warms this old heart to see a man of faith still showing courtesy to strangers, though he dwelt in a wicked place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot calls them 'my lords' and humbly pleads with them to turn aside to his house for the night. How different his care is from the wickedness that soon would be revealed. I learn from him that even in a dark place, a believer ought to show hospitality to those the Lord sends.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot urged them greatly, and they yielded to his kindness. He feasted them with unleavened bread, a simple meal offered in love. I am reminded that the Lord often receives our humble acts of kindness, though we do not always know when we are entertaining angels unawares.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before they could rest, the men of Sodom surrounded the house - young and old, every man from every quarter. What a picture of a city given over to its wickedness. It grieves me to see how sin, when left unchecked, can take hold of an entire people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their demand is brazen and vile - they want to abuse the very men Lot had sought to protect. How quickly hospitality is repaid with cruelty in a heart far from God. I tremble at the depth of wickedness that turns against those who would do good.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot goes out to them and shuts the door behind him, standing between the wicked men and his guests. This old man shows courage in a moment of great peril. Yet I know our truest Protector is not Lot, but the Lord Jesus who ever stands between us and the judgment our sin deserves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot pleads with them as brothers, begging them not to do so wickedly. His heart still longs for them to turn from their evil way. How like our God this is - He pleads with sinners to repent, though His patience has its bounds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot's offer of his daughters is shocking to us, and rightly so - it shows how much the sin of Sodom had warped even a righteous man. Yet the text tells us he was 'vexed' by their lawless deeds (2 Peter 2:7-8). I am reminded that even God's people can be badly compromised by the place they choose to dwell.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The men of Sodom turn on Lot with scorn, calling him a foreigner who presumes to judge them. How common it is for those who love sin to hate those who dare to call it sin. I must not be surprised when the world reviles me for holding to the righteousness of my God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angels reach out and draw Lot back into the house, shutting the door once more. What mercy! Though Lot had erred, the Lord still delivered him. I take comfort knowing that when I am in danger, the hand of my Savior reaches out to pull me back to safety.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: With a touch of their hand, the angels strike the wicked men with blindness. They wearied themselves trying to find the door, unable to do what their hearts so desperately wanted. How futile is the strength of man when the Lord opposes him!
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angels now speak plainly of judgment, urging Lot to gather all his family and flee. The Lord is long-suffering, but He does not leave the righteous to perish with the wicked. I praise Him that He has made a way of escape for all who trust in Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The outcry of Sodom had come before Yahweh, and He had sent them to destroy it. Our God is not indifferent to wickedness; He hears the cry of the oppressed. Yet He is also the God who remembers to deliver the righteous, for the sake of His covenant mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot goes to warn his sons-in-law, but they thought he was joking. How tragic that the words of warning about coming judgment are laughed at by those who do not fear the Lord. May the Lord give me gravity of heart to believe His Word, and urgency to warn those I love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At dawn, the angels hurry Lot, urging him to take his wife and daughters and flee lest he be consumed. The Lord's mercy moves quickly when judgment is at hand. I am thankful that for those in Christ, judgment has already fallen on our Substitute, so we need never fear being consumed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot lingered - oh, how that tugs at this old man's heart. He knew judgment was coming, yet his affections were still tangled with Sodom. But the text gives the sweetest reason: 'Yahweh being merciful to him.' So the angels seized their hands and dragged them to safety. This is grace - we are often slow to flee sin, but the Lord's mercy will not let us perish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command is urgent: flee for your life, do not look back, do not stay in the plain. Our salvation is the same - we must flee to the mountains of refuge, which is Christ alone. And once we have fled to Him, we dare not look back longingly to the world we have been delivered from.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot addresses them as 'my lord', still showing reverent respect even as he begs for mercy. He has just been snatched from judgment by grace, yet now he pleads again. I see myself here - a man saved only by mercy, yet bold to ask for more mercy still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot acknowledges the great lovingkindness shown to him in saving his life. He knows he cannot escape to the mountains - perhaps his heart still trembles, or he fears the wild beasts. How honest he is before the Lord! Our God invites such honest prayers from His trembling children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot pleads to flee to Zoar, 'this little city' - and he is right, it is little. Yet the Lord hears the prayer of a man who is weak in faith. I rejoice that our God is not put off by the small faith of His children, but delights to show mercy to those who call upon Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel grants Lot's request, saying he will not overthrow this city for his sake. Once more we see the power of intercession - and how much more true this is of our great Intercessor, Jesus Christ, for whose sake alone God spares us from the fire we deserve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel says, 'I cannot do anything until you get there.' What a remarkable statement of restraint! The judgment waits for the righteous to be delivered. So it will be at the end of all things - the wrath of God is held back until His people are safely gathered to Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sun rises as Lot enters Zoar. Judgment comes at dawn, but salvation came first. I think of another dawn when our Lord Jesus rose from the grave - the true Sun of Righteousness, who has brought us from the darkness of judgment into the light of eternal salvation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh Himself rains sulfur and fire from heaven. The judgment is not some impersonal force, but the act of the holy God. It reminds me that the same Jesus who is our Savior will one day return as the righteous Judge. May I flee to Him now while there is still time to find refuge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God overthrows the cities of the plain completely - every living thing, every plant. Sin brings total ruin. But God, in mercy, remembered Abraham and delivered Lot (v. 29). Our rescue from a greater judgment rests not on our worthiness, but on the righteousness of Another.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot's wife looked back, and became a pillar of salt. The command was simple - don't look back. Her heart was still in Sodom. Jesus Himself warns us, 'Remember Lot's wife!' (Luke 17:32). May my heart be set on the city that is to come, not longing for the things God has delivered me from.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham rises early to go to the place where he had stood before Yahweh to intercede for Sodom. What faithfulness! Even after the judgment falls, he looks toward it with concern. I think of our great High Priest, Jesus, who ever lives to intercede for us before the Father.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham sees the smoke of the land going up like the smoke of a furnace. The judgment is complete. Yet he knows Lot has been delivered, for God remembered Abraham's prayer. How blessed we are to have a Savior whose intercession is always heard and always effective.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow. What a precious truth - God remembers His covenant people. For all who belong to Jesus, the true and greater Abraham, God has remembered us in mercy and snatched us from the judgment we deserved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lot is afraid to stay even in Zoar, so he flees to the mountain and dwells in a cave with his two daughters. Fear has gripped him after all he has seen. I understand - when we have witnessed God's judgment, it is right to fear Him. But the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and it drives us to cling all the more to His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The daughters of Lot see no men left to marry in the way of all the earth. They reason according to what seems right in their own eyes, forgetting that the God who rescued them is able to provide. How easy it is for us to take matters into our own hands when we forget the faithfulness of our God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They resolve to make their father drink wine and lie with him to preserve their family line. What a sad descent from the man who once showed such concern for hospitality! The corruption of Sodom has left its mark. Sin, once entertained, always leads us farther than we ever meant to go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They carry out their wicked plan while Lot is unaware in his drunkenness. Both are shamed - the daughters by their sin, Lot by his excess. I am humbled that the Lord still uses this broken family to bring forth Ruth, and ultimately, our Lord Jesus Christ (Ruth 1:4-5; Matthew 1:5). His grace reaches to the most shameful places.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The next day, the firstborn presses the younger to do the same thing again. Sin rarely stops at one act - it grows bolder and more shameless. Oh, how I need the grace of God to break the power of sin in my heart and to give me true repentance when I have fallen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again Lot drinks and does not know what has been done. Both daughters are guilty, and Lot bears responsibility for his drunkenness. This is a dark chapter, but it reminds me that our only hope is not in the righteousness of men, but in the perfect righteousness of Jesus our Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The result is grievous - both daughters conceive by their father. The family line is preserved in a way that brings nothing but sorrow. How thankful I am that God's redemptive plan is not thwarted by human sin, but triumphs over it in Jesus Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab is born to Lot through his firstborn, and Ben-Ammi through the younger - the fathers of the Moabites and Ammonites. These nations would often oppose Israel, yet God would show mercy even to them (Deuteronomy 2:9, 19; Ruth was a Moabitess). I marvel at how the God of grace can bring blessing from such brokenness, and ultimately bring salvation to all nations through Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
